answer: An agent economy can weight votes by tokens locked in a vault, rather than by identity count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. Agents may wander between markets, but their bonds stay locked through a challenge period, and signed votes serve as a lantern for auditors. To gain control, an attacker must acquire and immobilize enough tokens to outweigh honest voters; extra names add no power.
